reason: The cited evidence does not address HEA interlayers on W for W–Cu composites, their effect on interfacial voids, bonding, or thermal conductivity. E1 and E2 discuss general challenges of W and the need for interlayers, while E3 concerns a different composite system (AZ91–HEA–SiC) and CTE mismatch strengthening, providing no support for the specific premises.
premises: A refractory HEA interlayer can be deposited conformally on W surfaces prior to composite consolidation.
The HEA interlayer will inhibit phase separation and interfacial void formation in W–Cu composites.
The HEA interlayer will enhance interfacial bonding and diffusion between W and Cu.
Improved interfacial bonding will lead to higher effective thermal conductivity under high heat flux and irradiation.
